subject.title: fix(auto-reply): prevent reply hook memory growth during bursts

question: Should exact-correlated reply usageState become intentionally lossy once more than 1,024 snapshots are awaiting consumption?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound and preserves public types, but the fixed capacity introduces a new observable omission case for plugin hook consumers that requires ownership acceptance.

options.title: Accept bounded degradation
options.body: Merge the 1,024-entry oldest-first bound because usageState is optional best-effort metadata and unbounded Gateway memory growth is the worse failure mode.

options.title: Carry metadata directly
options.body: Pause this patch and redesign the delivery path to carry each snapshot with its run state, avoiding both a global capacity limit and correlated metadata loss at greater implementation cost.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded degradation
recommendation.body: Merge the 1,024-entry oldest-first bound because usageState is optional best-effort metadata and unbounded Gateway memory growth is the worse failure mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged feature history ties this person most directly to the exact-run handoff design and its contract repairs.
